messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: OKR velocity reset — scope trims, infra unblock asks, and QBR artifacts

Team — quick leadership check-in as we land on the middle of the quarter and prep QBR artifacts. Short version up front: two initiatives need scope reduction or we will miss delivery targets; we also need a concrete unblock on GPU infra for 2 weeks to finish the autoscaling validator. I outlined asks and tradeoffs below. Please reply with commitments by EOD Monday.

1) Status highlights (objective: Improve inference cost per req by 20%)
- Embedding cache (owner: infra/opt): currently ~60% through implementation; rollout blocked by low-memory regression in quantized model profile. Risk: will push measurable savings into next quarter if not fixed.
- GenServe autoscaling (owner: runtime): feature 70% done, integration tests failing under sustained burst. Blocker is access to 8x A100 pool for another 2 weeks to run soak tests.
- Eval suite: examples show a 1.5% quality drift when using 4-bit quant; need one more round of focused prompts.

2) Ask: scope trims we should consider (pick one by EOD):
- Option A (safer): Defer noncritical retraining and keep embedding cache MVP (trim search-result freshness window).
- Option B (aggressive): Defer cache rollout and focus infra hours on autoscale validator soak tests.

3) Infra unblock request:
- Requesting dedicated 8x A100 for 14 days (dev-tagged pool). Owner: Marcus — can you confirm availability and cost delta? I attached cost-impact-brief.xlsx and dependency_matrix.csv.

4) QBR artifacts needed by Wed: short one-page callouts for each OKR (I uploaded a checklist to the drive link). I can draft the product-facing slide but need precise metrics from runtime and infra.

Attachments: QBR_artifacts_list.pdf, dependency_matrix.csv, cost-impact-brief.xlsx

Why this matters: if we keep both initiatives full-scope we risk missing the cost target and delaying enterprise ROI messaging for BrightBank (they're expecting a cost delta in the QBR).

Next steps: mark which option you prefer (A/B) and whether you can spare headcount or infra for the soak window.

Thanks — Naomi

Naomi — thanks for the concise callout. Quick responses inline: 

- Option preference: leaning Option A unless Marcus confirms the A100 window without material cost push. Option A keeps us able to show partial wins in the QBR.
- Headcount: I can free up one SRE (Chris) for two weeks to help with the mem-regression root cause if we choose Option A. He can start Tuesday.
- QBR metrics: I'll pull the per-route latency and cost-to-serve numbers from the console and drop into the drive doc by EOD Wednesday.

One ask: if we choose Option B, we should notify Sales (BrightBank) with a short note that we are shifting timelines for their cache rollout. If they object, we revert to A.

— Vanessa

Naomi/Team — I can provision the 8x A100 pool but there are two constraints: finance needs a short approval (estimated incremental spend ~$18k for the 14-day window) and we need to shift two low-priority jobs off the pool. I can temporarily reassign those jobs.

If we go Option B and run soak tests, we'll accelerate autoscale integration but Embedding cache gets delayed by ~3 weeks. Given BrightBank's ask for cost improvements in QBR, my recommendation is Option A + SRE support (Vanessa's offer). That gives us some immediate wins for the QBR and buys time to do rigorous soak testing in the follow-up sprint.

I'll open a finance approval ticket and tag SUP-123 (JIRA-SUP-123). Can Finance expedite? Laura — can you help route the approval?
